issues.item: Threat from Strangers: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
issues.explanation: For physical abuse by a romantic partner, the threat profile is centered on generalized danger from strangers, while the appraisals are centered on bodily damage/shame and permanent emotional change. This is not impossible, but as the only represented components it is clinically hard to integrate into a single coherent profile of partner abuse without any partner-specific or trauma-linked threat content.

issues.item: Body Shame: I feel ashamed of what happened to my body
issues.explanation: Within the formulation, the only active links are between Negative Appraisals and Threat, so these two nodes should strongly cohere. Here the negative appraisals imply consequences focused on the body and self after intimate physical abuse, but the threat item 'threat from strangers approaching me' points to a different danger representation that is not reflected in the appraisals. That weakens the expected tight appraisal-threat coupling.

vignette:
Leilani, an 80-year-old woman of Oceanic descent, had built a life around the precision and strength demanded by her lifelong trade as a welder, a skill she still practiced part-time. Yet, for years, an insidious unease had tightened its grip, a constant companion that stole her peace. Decades ago, she had endured a brutal physical assault at the hands of a romantic partner, an event that had left not just physical scars, but an indelible mark on her sense of self and safety. She remembered the sudden, overwhelming force, the feeling of her body being utterly beyond her control, and the deep, pervasive pain that followed.

In the aftermath, Leilani had come to believe that her body had been permanently damaged by what happened, a profound conviction that settled deep within her. This appraisal, the sense that she could no longer trust her own body to keep her safe or to recover fully, became a lens through which she viewed the world. She became convinced that she would never be able to feel normal emotions again, that the capacity for simple joy or peace had been irrevocably lost. This deeply held belief in her own physical vulnerability and the unreliability of her body fed a pervasive sense of threat. She found herself constantly on edge, struggling to quiet her mind at night, experiencing significant trouble falling or staying asleep. Even in the quiet solitude of her own home, she felt profoundly on guard, an internal alarm system perpetually set to high alert.

The constant state of vigilance, in turn, intensified her negative beliefs about herself and her future. Each night, Leilani would wake during the night to check whether she was safe, her heart pounding, scanning the room for any perceived danger. This relentless pattern of being alert at home and the repeated experience of waking to check her surroundings served as powerful, daily evidence that her body was indeed unreliable, always on the verge of breakdown or attack. It confirmed her fear that she truly would never be able to feel normal emotions again, as true peace seemed forever out of reach. The physical demands of her welding work, once a source of pride, now often brought a wave of anxiety; the heavy equipment and the need for steady hands sometimes made her acutely aware of her body’s perceived fragility, reinforcing the idea that it had been permanently damaged.

The cycle had tightened over the years, impacting her marriage to her current, loving husband, who often found her distant or preoccupied, her mind caught in a loop of apprehension. She would sometimes flinch at a sudden clang from a dropped tool in her workshop or recoil from a quick movement made by her husband, even though she knew logically he posed no threat. What frightened Leilani most was the sense of entrapment, the feeling that this relentless internal battle would define the rest of her life. It was this creeping despair, this profound exhaustion from constantly being on guard, that finally led her to seek help, hoping to reclaim some semblance of the emotional normalcy she felt she had lost so long ago.
